findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: Propagating the store error does not make limit enforcement persistent: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and leaves that entry in place when ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned. The first request from an over-limit device is rejected, but a retry with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil, and successfully authenticates for the next 29 minutes. Cache devices only after successful admission, and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

findings.title: Make the device count check and admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or transaction that serializes admissions. When one slot remains, concurrent requests with different device IDs can all observe a count below deviceLimit and all insert successfully. Those devices then remain eligible for updates even though the configured limit has been exceeded. Serialize the count-and-insert operation across instances using database-level coordination, and test concurrent admissions at the limit.
